_README: THE WITHDRAWAL REGISTER. A retired figure or claim is DECLARED here, by id, and
`eval/tools/docstat.py --withdrawn` asserts that no LIVE document states it outside a
block that cites that id. Read `_check_withdrawal_register` in docstat.py for the rule
and for what it cannot see.
WHY DECLARED AND NOT INFERRED. The obvious alternative - a cross-document
figure-agreement check - was built and measured under task 11 and comes out against:
52 labelled figures over six live docs, 1 disagreement, and that one a false positive.
It cannot see a stale figure, because the restatements of a stale figure AGREE to the
digit. Propagation and consistency are the same observation (#113). What separates a
live figure from a retired one is not in the numbers; it is whether a withdrawal was
ever declared, which is a fact about the record and has to be written down.
APPEND-ONLY. An entry is never deleted and never edited to say something else. It is a
record of a decision that was made, and a consumer that applied it must keep being able
to. Add `reinstated` with a date and a reason if a withdrawal is itself reversed.
FIELDS
id           the exemption key. A live document may state the entry freely inside any
block that carries this string. Nothing else exempts anything - not a
file, not a line number, not a marker word.
match        every one of these regexes must occur inside one block for that block to
count as stating the entry. ALL, not any: a single loose pattern would
fire on unrelated prose.
anchor       an ARCHIVE file where the entry is stated in full and correctly. The
check proves its own extraction here before trusting it anywhere: an
entry that matches nothing in its anchor is reporting its own silence,
and is a failure, not a pass (AGENTS.md rule 12).
declared_in  where the withdrawal is argued, for a person.
replaced_by  what to state instead. A withdrawal with no replacement leaves the next
author with the same gap that produced the bad figure.

entries.claim: tier 3's separation result stated as 'between-stack range of mean ranks 1.70, mean gap 2.05'
entries.why: It named no population - no run, no game, no aspect set, no date - and reproduces under no method. The only field tier 3 has judged gives 1.900/2.275 pre-repair and 2.100/1.925 post-repair on rank/pool, and the quantity has two free method parameters, so there are four readings per field and 1.70/2.05 is none of the eight.
entries.replaced_by: eval/judge/field_ranks.py --rounds eval/runs/wg-tetris-judge-2026-08-17/pre (and /post). Quote value=rank order=pool, and name the field: 1.900 against 2.275 pre-repair, 2.100 against 1.925 post-repair.

entries.claim: finding #54 - `architecture` and `ux` share no evidence and rank the field identically on both presentation orders, so their agreement evidences a shared prior
entries.why: The claim rested on tau 1.00 across two presentation orders of ONE round, which is one observation reported twice. The repeat, with ux's evidence provably unchanged, gives tau 0.385 (seed 0, 13 comparable pairs) and 0.667 (seed 1, 12). The redundant pairs the second round does find are different ones and agree with neither.
entries.declared_in: eval/findings/certifies-nothing.md, finding #54, section 'WITHDRAWN 2026-08-17'; and eval/judge/JUDGING.md, 'RESULT after the repairs'
entries.replaced_by: What survives is the method, not the result: giving two judges disjoint evidence and checking they disagree is still the cheapest detector for a shared prior, but a positive reading needs repeats at a FIXED order (#58). Do not cite #54 as evidence of anything.

entries.claim: the project's scale stated as '24 whole-game submissions, three games, four stacks, two independent trials per cell'
entries.why: Each count was true of wg-matrix-2026-08-13 alone and the sentence named no population, so as written it describes nothing that can be checked. Over the population it appeared to claim - every stored trial record carrying a `game` field - the tree holds 90 records in 11 run directories, 4 games, 4 stacks, and a pooled game x stack cell of 4 to 8 trials, not 2. Nothing in the repository produced any of the four numbers, which is why they outlived their scope by three runs; the cost half of the same sentence had the identical shape and was 34% low.
entries.declared_in: README.md, the notice under the counts table; task 64
entries.replaced_by: python3 eval/tools/census.py, which prints every count with the population it was counted over and exits 2 rather than reporting 0. Quote the matrix scope for replication - wg-matrix-2026-08-13 is 24 records = 3 games x 4 stacks x 2 trials per cell - and never the pooled tree, whose runs mostly may not be compared (eval/RUNS.md).

entries.claim: the deterministic tiers stated as '20 of 24 cells score exactly 1.000'
entries.why: It never said which 24 cells it counted. Eight different combinations of three 8-cell groups give exactly 20/24, and they disagree about which games and which runs are included - some spanning regime boundaries the docs elsewhere declare void. Summing across games is separately barred: the play-bot scores 13 criteria on pong and 22 on arena, so a 1.000 is a different achievement per column (#72).
entries.declared_in: README.md corrections table; tasks/05-state-the-criterion-count-disparity-as-its-o.md `established_by`; eval/IMPROVEMENTS.md, 'the test has fired five times'
entries.replaced_by: Per game, never summed. wg-matrix-2026-08-13: pong 5/8, tetris 5/8, arena 5/8. wg-audio48: pong 8/8, tetris 8/8. wg-g4c platformer: 6/8. Those counts are of stored `overall` under the pre-2026-08-23 weighted scheme and do not cross the tier-1-becomes-a-gate boundary recorded in eval/RUNS.md - state the scheme with the count.

entries.claim: the within-cell agreement stated as '0 verdict differences across 380 paired criteria'
entries.why: Both halves fail. The 2026-08-22 recount searched every coherent scope - all runs 1098 paired, wg-matrix alone 436, wg-matrix+wg-arena3d 584, wg-audio48 232, everything-except-g4 958, and by tier playbot 540 and programmatic 402 - and NONE gives 380. Six arbitrary subsets do, each mixing runs and games incoherently. And '0 verdict differences' is false in every scope with a plausible count: 5 for wg-matrix, 13 across all runs. Part of that drift is this project's own criterion repairs re-grading cells, so it may have been true when written - which is the argument for recording an aggregate's scope AND its date.
entries.replaced_by: The PRODUCER, not a figure: python3 eval/judge/paired_verdicts.py --runs-root <main checkout>/eval/runs, which counts per (run, game) and per tier set and prints the tier set beside every row. Its 5 corpus pins reproduce the scoped recount this entry was replaced by - wg-matrix all tiers 436 paired / 5 verdict / 332 evidence, wg-audio48 all tiers 232 / 0 / 120 - and that pair may NOT support a claim about the deterministic tiers, because 156 of wg-matrix's 436 are LLM-judge criteria at weight 0.00 and wg-audio48's 232 contains none. Deterministic-only the same runs read 280 / 4 / 176 and 232 / 0 / 120. Quote a (run, game) row with its tier set; the pooled counts are counts, never rates. DECISIONS.md carries the nine-group table.

entries.claim: the within-cell evidence control stated as '219 of 380 evidence strings differ (58%)'
entries.why: It is the denominator of WR-paired-verdict-tie and dies with it: no coherent scope over the stored reports yields 380 paired criteria, so no scope yields 219 of them. The control it performs - showing the two trials in a cell are genuinely different artifacts - survives, but only per scope.
entries.replaced_by: The PRODUCER: python3 eval/judge/paired_verdicts.py --runs-root <main checkout>/eval/runs prints an e-diff column per (run, game) per tier set. Over the 9 stored (run, game) groups, DETERMINISTIC tiers only, the evidence-difference rate runs 48.8% (41 of 84) to 66.9% (99 of 148); the ALL-TIER per-run readings this entry was replaced by, wg-matrix 332 of 436 and wg-audio48 120 of 232, are among its pins. Quote a group with its tier set, never the pool.

entries.claim: the stored tree stated as 137 trial records over 19 run directories carrying $2,404.21 of agent trials, and its spec-change half as 47 records over 8 directories carrying $91.72
entries.why: Every one of those was census.py's one-level `*/trials/*.json` glob reporting its own reach. eval/runs/archive-run1-byte-identical-prompts/ is a wrapper holding four run directories one level deeper, so 24 records - 15% of the tree, all of them spec-change - were dropped with no diagnostic. The tree holds 161 records over 23 run directories and $2,466.31; the spec-change half is 71 over 12 and $153.82. The cross-check that certified the figure in task 64 was eval/RUNS.md, whose source column names the same one-level glob run by hand, so the agreement was two readings of one blind spot (#37, #126). DECISIONS.md, eval/AGENTS.md and #122 had said 71 over 12 all along.
entries.declared_in: README.md, the second notice under the counts table; eval/findings/certifies-nothing.md, finding #126; task 69
entries.replaced_by: python3 eval/tools/census.py, which now searches at any depth, identifies a run by its path relative to runs/, and prints how many trials/*.json it skipped as agent-authored. 161 records over 23 run directories, $2,466.31; whole-game 90 over 11, $2,312.49; spec-change 71 over 12, $153.82. The whole-game figures are unchanged by the repair - no whole-game run is nested - so only the tree and spec-change rows were ever wrong.

entries.claim: the size of the findings log stated as 'Thirty-seven numbered findings', opening README's 'The one thing this project actually learned'
entries.why: The log held 113 numbered findings, #19-#131, when this was withdrawn. The figure was written when it was true and nothing in the repository produced it, so nothing could disagree: the range sentence 360 lines above it was gated and correct, and a range is not a count - #19-#131 is equally true of 113 findings and of 40. It was also spelled in WORDS, which is the second reason it survived eleven merges past a table telling every author to run a producer: no check can compare a cardinal it cannot parse. The claim the figure introduces - that all but a few findings are instances of one pattern - is unaffected and stands.
entries.declared_in: task 88; README.md's 'The one thing this project actually learned' section now states the produced count beside its command
entries.replaced_by: python3 eval/tools/docstat.py --findings, which counts eval/findings/ and eval/FINDINGS.md independently, prints the population it counted over, exits 2 rather than reporting 0, and exits 1 when the two sources or any live document disagree.

entries.claim: the three g1_pong round-1 judge calls of 2026-08-16 stated as '$13.15, mean $4.38 per field call'
entries.why: It is the losing half of a two-way disagreement about ONE quantity, and not a rounding difference: 13.15/3 rounds to 4.38 and 13.16/3 rounds to 4.39, so each document was internally consistent and the two disagreed about the SUM. Neither can be re-read - these are the only judge rounds in the project with no surviving artifact (task 04), and judge_ledger.py --tree runs/ reads 97 rounds over 12 directories with none of them this field. The tie is decided anyway, by the ledger table that prints the figure: its g2_tetris3d rows sum to $33.63, which judge_ledger.py still re-derives to the cent from wg-tetris-judge-2026-08-17/pre/, and 46.79 - 33.63 = 13.16 exactly, where $13.15 would require a day total of $46.78. That is coherence with a published total rather than a re-reading, since $46.79 has no artifact either - but only $13.15 contradicts the table it was printed beside. The recorded per-call range $2.82-$5.29 discriminates neither: the third call is $5.05 under one and $5.04 under the other.
entries.declared_in: eval/RUNS.md, the note under the specialist-judge ledger table; DECISIONS.md, 'The g1_pong round-1 judge figure is $13.16, mean $4.39'; task 130
entries.replaced_by: $13.16 for the 3 calls and $4.39 for the mean, defined once in eval/RUNS.md's specialist-judge ledger together with the rounding rule - cents round half-up, never truncate. These 3 calls of 2026-08-16 cannot be reconstructed - their artifacts are gone - so no producer can re-derive THIS figure; that is a statement about these calls, not about judge costs in general, which judge_ledger.py produces from every round still on disk. The mean is a RETROSPECTIVE AGGREGATE and not a rate: it averages architecture and idiomatic over 3 calls, and per-aspect rates on g2_tetris3d span $0.60 to $6.81 a call, so nothing may be projected from it (AGENTS.md rule 4) - price a sweep from a (game, aspect) row of that same table instead, treating 2 calls as a lower bound. judge_ledger.py prints no per-call mean for this reason, and the 1 projection made from this one came out 1.84x low.

entries.claim: the tier-3 separation pair on wg-tetris-judge-2026-08-17/pre stated as rank+pool 1.900 against 2.275
entries.why: It was pooled over five aspects, one of which - `idiomatic` - has been barred from any cross-stack ranking since #53, and a pooled figure IS a between-stack range. `field_ranks.assert_poolable` now refuses a barred aspect exactly as it refuses a control (tasks/146), so the producer cannot return this pair again. Note that WR-tier3-pair's `replaced_by` field names this superseded population; it is a record of a 2026-08-22 decision and is not edited.
entries.declared_in: eval/RUNS.md, 'THE TIER-3 POOLED POPULATION CHANGED ON 2026-08-24'
entries.replaced_by: python3 eval/judge/field_ranks.py --rounds eval/runs/wg-tetris-judge-2026-08-17/pre, value=rank order=pool over the 4 poolable aspects: 1.3125 against 2.5625.

entries.why: Same defect as WR-tier3-pool-pre: pooled over five aspects including the cross-stack-barred `idiomatic`. This pair also carried the only 'between exceeds within' direction the project quoted under its own reporting method; over the 4 poolable aspects the direction reverses.
